argument.text: Use H001. For E002 take arbitrary I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1 and lambda=0 for the X estimate. X gives precisely L-infinity L2 and L-infinity H^(-23/14) derivative, its hypotheses. Its three choices of negative-norm slot are retained. For constant inputs use E002 with any lambda in [0,1]. Each source spatial norm is sqrt(2 pi) times ours: divide by sqrt(2 pi) on the output and absorb the remaining product factors 2 pi into the constant. This proves the first two assertions without changing their exponent or time length. Smooth or continuous piecewise smooth time functions have the stated distributional derivative, so E002 applies directly. General X inputs use the source bounded interpretation of the operator. When a=b the integral is zero, so the zero-length interval case follows directly. The negative spatial norm is finite for X inputs: since <k>>=1, the weights <k>^(-2pstar) are at most 1, and termwise comparison of D003's nonnegative squared Fourier sums gives ||h||_{H^(-pstar)}<=||h||_2, also in time L-infinity. D019 supplies the bounded extension interpretation, and D020 supplies the distributional derivative for continuous piecewise time-smooth inputs.

produces.statement: For every I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1 and fj in X(I), ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||fj||_X+C||fi||_{L-infinity H^(-pstar)} product_{j!=i}||fj||_{L-infinity L2}, for each i in {1,2,3}. For time-independent fj in H^lambda and 0<=lambda<=1, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_lambda |I|^lambda product_j||fj||_{H^lambda}; at |I|=0 the integral is zero. Constants are uniform in interval location and support, and the bounded interpretation agrees with smooth inputs.

argument.text: H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply the product inequality in E003 with lambda=gamma and, when gamma=1/2, epsilon=1/8. This is permitted because 1/8>0 and the product inequality allows any fixed positive epsilon. The source exponent a(lambda) is exactly a_gamma by its definition. Consequently ||fg||_2<=C_gamma ||f||_{H^gamma}||g||_{H^{a_gamma}} for arbitrary f in H^gamma and g in H^{a_gamma}. Dividing by sqrt(2 pi) converts the source output norm to the D003 norm and leaves just the fixed factor sqrt(2 pi) on the right, absorbed into C_gamma. For the stage estimate at lambda=1/2, the phrase 'arbitrary fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0' in E003 asserts a positive threshold such that every smaller positive loss is admissible. There is a positive loss below both this threshold and 1/8: take half the smaller of these two positive numbers. E003 therefore gives the existence of a real stageLossLocal in (0,1/8] such that, for every beta in [-1/2-stageLossLocal,3/2], every mean-zero time-independent q1,q2 in H^{1/2}, t_n>=0, tau>0 and t in [t_n,t_n+tau], the source norms satisfy ||(1/2) integral_{t_n}^t B_s(q1,q2) ds||_{H^beta}<=C_{beta,stageLossLocal} tau^((3/2-beta)/(2+stageLossLocal)) ||q1||_{H^{1/2}}||q2||_{H^{1/2}}. The constants depend only on beta and the loss. This loss can be chosen independently of the step and input data.

produces.statement: There exists a real stageLossLocal with 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8 such that for all mean-zero time-independent q1,q2 in H^{1/2}, every t_n>=0, tau>0, t in [t_n,t_n+tau], and beta in [-1/2-stageLossLocal,3/2], one has ||(1/2) integral_{t_n}^t B_s(q1,q2) ds||_{H^beta} <= C_{beta,stageLossLocal} tau^((3/2-beta)/(2+stageLossLocal)) ||q1||_{H^{1/2}}||q2||_{H^{1/2}}, using source unnormalized norms. The constant depends only on beta and stageLossLocal, and is uniform in the inputs, step location, step size, step time and Fourier support.

For every productLeftLocal in H^gamma and productRightLocal in H^{a_gamma}, ||productLeftLocal productRightLocal||_2<=C_gamma ||productLeftLocal||_{H^gamma}||productRightLocal||_{H^{a_gamma}}, in the normalized Fourier Sobolev norms, with a constant depending only on gamma and the fixed product loss 1/8 at gamma=1/2.

argument.text:
Choose stageLossLocal as in F002, once and independently of all step data. Fix arbitrary mean-zero w in H^gamma, a bound ||w||_{H^gamma}<=M, t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1 and t in I_n=[t_n,t_n+tau], retaining these antecedents throughout the conclusion. Since gamma>0, comparison of the D003 Fourier weights gives ||w||_2<=||w||_{H^gamma}, so the inputs also lie in the domain of B. In E003 take lambda=gamma and f1=f2=w. Only in the middle stage case substitute the source loss epsilon=stageLossLocal. By D022 the resulting diagonal stage G_n(t;w,w) equals F_n(t;w), because their defining integrals coincide. Define beta0=2gamma-3/2 if gamma<1/2, -1/2-stageLossLocal if gamma=1/2, and gamma-1 if gamma>1/2. For beta selected as a_gamma or 1+gamma put theta=(1+gamma-beta)/(1+gamma-beta0).
For beta=a_gamma, the range condition and exponent comparison follow case by case. If 0<gamma<1/2, then a_gamma-beta0=2-3gamma>0 and 1+gamma-a_gamma=1/2+2gamma>0. The denominator is 5/2-gamma>0 and theta=(1/2+2gamma)/(5/2-gamma). The inequality theta>=gamma follows from gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2=(gamma-1/4)^2+7/16>0. If gamma=1/2, then a_gamma remains 1/8, a_gamma-beta0=5/8+stageLossLocal>0 and 1+gamma-a_gamma=11/8>0. The denominator is 2+stageLossLocal, and theta=(11/8)/(2+stageLossLocal)=11/(16+8eta)>=11/17>1/2, since 0<stageLossLocal<=1/8. Thus this calculation uses the fixed target regularity 1/8 and the separately chosen admissible source loss stageLossLocal. If 1/2<gamma<=1, then a_gamma=0>=gamma-1=beta0, a_gamma<=1+gamma, the denominator is 2 and theta=(1+gamma)/2>=gamma. These exhaustive cases verify beta in [beta0,1+gamma] and theta>=gamma. E003 therefore gives ||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{a_gamma}}<=C tau^theta ||w||_{H^gamma}^2. Here and below constants are converted to our normalization: dividing each bilinear source estimate by sqrt(2 pi) leaves just the fixed factor sqrt(2 pi), absorbed into C. Because 0<tau<=1 and theta>=gamma, tau^theta=tau^gamma tau^(theta-gamma)<=tau^gamma. Also the norm antecedent implies M>=0 and ||w||_{H^gamma}^2<=M^2. Hence ||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{a_gamma}}<=C_M tau^gamma uniformly in t.
For beta=1+gamma the same source hypotheses hold. In the three cases the positive denominators 1+gamma-beta0 are respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+stageLossLocal and 2; beta is the upper endpoint, so theta=0. E003 gives ||F_n(t;w)||_{H^{1+gamma}}<=C ||w||_{H^gamma}^2<=C_M uniformly in t. Taking the supremum over I_n gives both asserted stage estimates. The fixed stageLossLocal can affect the constants but, being selected once from E003 at lambda=1/2, introduces no dependence on w, t_n, tau, t or Fourier support. All uses require only the stipulated H^gamma regularity. Universal introduction under the retained antecedents proves the stage clauses; together with F001 and F003 these prove the full asserted conclusion, with all stated uniformity and extension properties.

applications.bindings: Set lambda=0, [a,b]=I, and fj equal to the three given X(I) inputs. Apply the conclusion for each i=1,2,3.
hypothesis_checks: The arbitrary interval has 0<=a<=b and b-a<=1; lambda=0 is in [0,1].
X(I) supplies L-infinity L2 inputs and bounded H^(-23/14) distributional time derivatives. Thus these are exactly the source regularity conditions.

applications.bindings: Set lambda=gamma, epsilon=1/8 in the middle case; for the product choose arbitrary f in H^gamma and g in H^{a_gamma}.
hypothesis_checks: H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. At gamma=1/2, the product clause permits any fixed positive epsilon, so epsilon=1/8>0 is valid for this product application.
The product inputs are quantified in exactly these spaces. No stage instance is used in this application.

applications.bindings: Set lambda=gamma, f1=f2=w, beta=a_gamma; at gamma=1/2 set the source stage loss epsilon=stageLossLocal, the witness chosen from F002. The target a_gamma remains 1/8 in this case.
hypothesis_checks: H001 gives 0<gamma<=1. At gamma=1/2, F002 supplies an admissible stage loss stageLossLocal in (0,1/8], chosen at S003; the source loss is stageLossLocal. Admissibility comes from E003's sufficiently-small-loss quantifier, as derived in S002, rather than from positivity of a numerical loss.

The arbitrary w is time-independent, mean-zero and belongs to H^gamma with norm<=M; t_n>=0, 0<tau<=1 and t belongs to the step. The three calculations in S003 give a_gamma-beta0=2-3gamma>0, 5/8+stageLossLocal>0, or 1-gamma>=0 respectively, and a_gamma<=1+gamma. Thus beta=a_gamma lies in the source interval.

The same mean-zero time-independent H^gamma input w and step satisfy the source conditions. beta=1+gamma is the upper endpoint and beta0<=beta since the denominators 5/2-gamma, 2+stageLossLocal, and 2 are positive. The time exponent is zero.

The constant inputs have the stipulated H^lambda norms and zero time derivatives. For a=b the integral is zero directly.
